jobs.occupation: Strategic Funding Officer for a world-leading quantum computing programme
jobs.description:
About Us

  NQCP is an ambitious and diverse international programme, located at the Niels Bohr Institute at University of Copenhagen. We are building a world-leading quantum computing programme, that will drive research and innovation at multiple levels, from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to solutions for the quantum-classical control and readout interface, and all the way to quantum algorithms and applications. 

  The programme is supported by Quantum Foundry Copenhagen, a company focused on enabling QPU  fabrication, and assembly and packaging technologies.

  Our program mission is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  About the Role
 We are looking for a Strategic Funding Officer to support the programme in securing external funding and building impactful scientific and industrial development collaborations. The role combines scientific pre-award grant support, strategic fundraising, and facilitation of interdisciplinary partnerships.

  A key responsibility is to identify opportunities for synergy across research groups and bring scientists together to develop competitive collaborative and consortium-based grant applications.

  The role requires you to work at the intersection of university research, innovation and industrial chip manufacturing. The position will eventually cover activities in both organizations, and activities related to Quantum Foundry Copenhagen will be contractually specified.  

  Key Responsibilities

   	
• Drive the programme’s external funding strategy for scientific and industrial collaborations. Identify and communicate relevant funding opportunities. 	
• Collaborate across research groups and organizations in developing high-quality grant proposals. 	
• Carry out writing for project proposals. 	
• Coordinate large and multidisciplinary funding applications including financial and technical reporting. 	
• Build partnerships with external researchers, funders, and stakeholders. 	
• Work closely with both the strategy team and communications to align funding activities.   Qualifications

   	
• Proven track record in securing substantial grants. 	
• Ability to work in Danish preferred. 	
• Experience setting up and managing research consortia involving academia and industry. 	
• Experience in supporting research applications, including EU calls. 	
• Strong understanding of research funding mechanisms. 	
• Excellent project management and communication skills. 	
• Strong stakeholder management and ability to advance our mission. 	
• Ability to engage and collaborate effectively with researchers across disciplines. 	
• MSc or PhD in a scientific discipline.    

  Personal Profile

  You can conceptualize and drive a strategy forward. You are also scientifically curious, highly organized, and excel at connecting people and ideas. You enjoy working across disciplines and can translate funding opportunities into successful collaborative research initiatives.

  The ideal candidate is deeply committed to our overall mission and brings a strong sense of ownership to their work. Rather than just fitting into a team, they actively raise the performance of those around them and take accountability for the success of both organizations.

   

  We offer
 A central role at the heart of NQCP’s mission, where you will help drive progress across two ambitious organizations. You will work closely with research and engineering teams, engage with key partners, and contribute to the broader quantum ecosystem. You will also have the possibility to engage directly in new collaborations established upon successful grant applications, e.g. as scientific coordinator.

   

  Life in Denmark is supported with strong social services (free universal healthcare, free/subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care institutions and excellent public schools). Our work culture is highly egalitarian and prioritises work-life balance. Dual-career families are common, and workplaces offer flexibility to help balance exciting careers and good family time. Danish cities are known for excellent infrastructure, such as extensive bike path networks. We can also offer a thriving food-scene, excellent museums, and beautiful natural scenery.

   

  Terms of salary and employment
 The employment and salary are made in accordance with the Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning academics in the state sector concluded between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

  Employment will be as Special or Senior Consultant. The salary is based on seniority and negotiation for salary supplement is possible. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). Expected starting date is 1 Febuary 2027. The working hours are 37 hours per week on average, and the working hours are flexible. 

  The position is limited to 31 December 2029, and the appointment will be subject to receipt of security clearance.

   

  Your application
 If you find the job interesting, please send an electronic application with attachment via Jobportalen (click on the link "Apply Now" at the bottom of the post) no later than 8 December 2026.

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

   

  Further questions
 Any questions about the position may be directed to CSO Jan Thomsen jwt@nbi.ku.dk, Head of Commercial Anil Slipsager Thilsted ath@qfcph.com or COO Helle Grunnet helle.grunnet@nbi.dk

   

  The Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen – or SCIENCE – is Denmark's largest science research and education institution with 4,000 employees and 9,700 Bachelor and Master's students in 12 departments. The Faculty has an annual budget of DKK 3 billion.

  Learn more about The Faculty of Science at www.science.ku.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in MRI radiofrequency detector development - DTU Space
jobs.description:
If you are passionate about advanced MRI technology and want to contribute to the next generation of medical imaging, this PhD position offers a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of radiofrequency detector development in collaboration with leading international researchers in Denmark and Australia.

A typical MRI scanner uses radiofrequency detectors to image water molecules. Imaging other molecules and nuclei requires additional new detectors and antennas. The objective of the PhD project is to demonstrate MR imaging of nuclei other than hydrogen by building MRI detectors and antennas, which can cover frequencies of multiple nuclei.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The main outcome of the project will be a broadband/multinuclear detector array, ready to be implemented in clinical environment. It is a cross-disciplinary project and collaboration with the Department of Health Technology at DTU as well as other national and international institutions, such as University of Queensland, Aarhus University Hospital, GE Healthcare, DRCMR and others is an essential part. 

The tasks and responsibilities include:

• Literature study and evaluation of different multi-frequency detector configurations and identifying the most promising;
• Develop efficient element decoupling strategies minimizing noise correlation between array elements;
• Design and implement multinuclear multichannel radiofrequency coil array for MRI;
• Imaging experiments:
• Coordinate efforts on mechanical and electrical safety tests end approval for clinical use;
• Disseminate the project results to the public and exchange of knowledge with society.
The applicant will take part in research-based teaching. 

Contributing to the development of a good work atmosphere and a thriving environment is essential.

The candidate should have a master’s degree in engineering, preferably in electrical engineering.

It is an advantage to have experience in

• High frequency circuit design, fabrication and testing;
• Use of VNAs, spectrum analysers, noise figure meters and other measurement equipment in circuit testing;
• High frequency circuit design software;
• MR technology.
The position also requires, that: 

• You are driven by pushing boundaries;
• You are motivated by both individual and team accomplishments;
• You thrive on collaboration and teamwork.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be conducted continuously.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures 

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date will be as soon as possible by mutual agreement with the candidate.

The primary workplace is at DTU Lyngby Campus and a longer stay of about 6 month is anticipated at University of Queensland, Australia.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Associate Prof. Vitaliy Zhurbenko

You can read more about the Electromagnetic Systems Division and the Department of Health Tech at https://www.healthtech.dtu.dk/Research/Research-Sections/Section-Magnetic-Resonance/Group-MRI-acquisition and www.space.dtu.dk 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU.

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. The Electromagnetic Systems Division holds expertise within radiofrequency engineering. It is our goal to ensure research and engineering training at the highest international level. The project will be conducted in close cooperation with DTU Health Tech.

DTU Space
The Institute has about 200 employees and is located in the greater Copenhagen area at the Lyngby Campus of the Technical University of Denmark together with 19 other institutes within the technical sciences. In the Astrophysics & Atmospheric Physics Division of the Department of Space Research and Space Technology (DTU Space), current focus areas cover exoplanets, large-scale structure of the universe, physics of compact objects, space weather, upper atmosphere physics and cosmo-climatology, as well as development of instrumentation, in particular high-energy instrumentation, i.e. X- and gamma ray detectors and optics. The division is currently active in the operation of instruments and data analysis from three satellites. The division also runs four instrumentation laboratories and hosts a center for space weather research and forecasts.

Lead engineering at a profitable, funded proptech while the team is still small enough to shape.

• Want to set the technical direction for a growing team and still ship code yourself?

• How would you keep a small team shipping to production many times a day, with review and testing that catch problems before customers do, without every decision landing on your desk?

• Where would you draw the line between what an AI agent should suggest and what it can do on a property owner’s behalf?

Sounds like you? Then you might be our next CTO!

A property owner with a portfolio of buildings has a practical question: which repairs belong in next year’s budget, and which can wait? At Proprty.ai, our models estimate the condition and remaining life of building components and the energy and CO2 effect of improving them. Our software turns those estimates into maintenance plans, and our AI agent, Tily, helps owners analyze their portfolios and take action!

Our product went live in 2024 and is used by customers in Denmark, Norway and Germany. We reached profitability by the end of 2025 and raised DKK 21 million in April 2026, and we are not planning to stop there!

There is still so much we can do to make it even better, and you could help shape the future of building maintenance and how engineering is run at Proprty.ai.

Product: TypeScript, React, and Next.js on Vercel, with Supabase (PostgreSQL, row-level security, storage).**

Data and models: Python and PySpark on Databricks (Azure, EU), Python model services, and LLM features on Azure OpenAI. We also run a customer API and an MCP server.

What you get to shape

The team and the code.

You'll lead our product engineering team, work closely with our data engineers and our Chief Data Science Officer, and keep building core features yourself. You might coach a developer through a tricky problem in the morning and ship a feature yourself that afternoon. You'll own engineering hiring as the team grows, from deciding which roles we need to choosing the people you want on the team.

How we build and ship.

You’ll own the platform’s architecture and how we test and release. We release to production many times a day. Your job is to keep that pace while making every release reliable and secure. When an urgent customer request competes with longer-term platform work, you’ll make the call and explain what comes first and why.

Shape what Tily can do next.

Our data scientists build models for building condition, remaining life, cost, and energy across several European markets. Together with our Chief Data Science Officer, you'll get those models in front of customers, decide what Tily may do on an owner's behalf, and use feedback from property owners, Sales, and Customer Success to choose the next problems to solve.

Change how we use AI ourselves.

Change how we use AI ourselves. Our engineers build with Claude Code and Cursor, AI agents review every pull request in our CI/CD pipeline, and agents take on routine work end to end so the team can ship faster. We keep looking for new ways AI can raise our pace, and you'll lead that.

We talk a lot (in a good way). When a problem gets tricky, we pull up a chair and pair on it. We like having a laugh while we figure things out.

What you’ll bring?

You've been CTO or head of engineering at a startup or scale-up while the product, the team, and the rules were still taking shape, and you can show what changed because you were there. You know when to open a pull request yourself, when to let another engineer make the call, and which shortcut will come back to bite you two releases from now.

You bring curiosity about our industry, our customers' problems, and the business acumen to understand how our product delivers business value, so that you can help facilitate features that drive outcomes and make our users' lives easier.

We’re AI-first (the name’s a bit of a giveaway). If you’ve built an agent or shipped an AI feature, we’d love to hear what happened after the demo. What did customers trust it to do, and where did they want the controls back? You’ll get to make those calls with Tily and figure out where AI helps our own engineers ship better software.

The core of what we consider for a candidate

• You’ve led an engineering team, coached developers, and hired people to join it.

• You’re keen to build AI agents that customers can put to work and to explore where AI makes your own team more effective.

• You still build full-stack features with React, TypeScript, and SQL. You can take a feature from technical design through thoughtful user experience to release, and measure what happens when customers get their hands on it.

• Fluent in English

Experience we’d love to hear about

• Taking an engineering team from a startup to a scale-up phase, understanding how and when to mature processes as the team scales, and how that looks different in this new AI era.

• Shipping an AI agent or feature into production. We’re especially curious about what you changed after people started using it.

• How you’ve spoken with customers and industry experts to help ensure we’re on the forefront of solving the right problems in our platform

• Your perspective on the role of a CTO as a thought leader.

• Working with PostgreSQL or Next.js, or building products for real estate or proptech.

Where we work

We spend 4 days a week together in our office near Rådhuspladsen. You’ll need to be based in the Copenhagen area, as we can’t offer relocation or visa sponsorship for this role.

New to proptech? That’s fine. If you’ve led engineers and still enjoy being one, we’d love to hear from you.

Questions? Reach out to Casper Høgh at Csh@ing.dk, who helps us land the right human for the job

Our hiring process

• 
Intro call with Casper Høgh – We’ll talk about your background, what you want from your next CTO role, and any questions you have about proprty.ai.

• 
In-person interview – Meet us at our Copenhagen office for a small demo and talk through the team, the decisions you’d own, and how you like to lead while staying hands-on.

• 
Case interview – Work through an engineering scenario with us. We want to understand what you’d prioritize, which trade-offs you see, and why.

• 
Board interview - Meet with one of our board members. Get their perspective on our journey and talk them through how you would help us in our next phase of growth.

• 
Offer – If we both see a fit, we’ll talk through the offer and next steps together.

TL;DR

Want to get in early with a great team? Love leading engineers and still writing code?

Apply now to lead our dev team and make building maintenance smarter and more sustainable with AI.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarships in machine learning for optimization of cyber-physical systems - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
We offer PhD scholarships at DTU Compute to develop machine learning methods for faster analysis and optimization of cyber-physical systems. You will build predictive models of expensive analytical calculations and simulations, and use AI to find good solutions to optimization problems that cannot be solved exactly within practical computing budgets. 

You will join the Embedded Systems Engineering section and work with Prof. Paul Pop. The application areas are related to, e.g., software-defined vehicles, datacenters, industrial automation, and energy systems.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will connect learned prediction models with optimization methods. The PhD topics will be defined with the supervisors. You will:

• Develop surrogate models that predict results of complex analyses and simulations, such as execution delays, energy use, and resource demands.
• Use machine learning to guide configuration, scheduling, and resource allocation, reducing the need for expensive model evaluations.
• Evaluate solution quality, computing time, uncertainty, and transfer to new systems; check proposed solutions against the original models and constraints.
• Publish your research, collaborate with project partners, and contribute to teaching and student supervision.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Ideally, you have both a BSc and an MSc in machine learning or artificial intelligence. Degrees in computer science, applied mathematics, electrical engineering, or related fields with substantial ML/AI coursework and projects are also relevant.

You should have a strong foundation in machine learning, algorithms, probability, and linear algebra; experience implementing and evaluating models in Python; and good written and spoken English. Experience with optimization, reinforcement learning, or simulation is an advantage. Prior expertise in all application areas is not required.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
Assessment will consider academic qualifications, machine learning and programming experience, research potential, and fit with the topic.

jobs.description:
The future of climate action extends beyond reducing emissions
Atmospheric CO2 concentrations continue to rise despite global efforts to reduce emissions. Achieving climate neutrality will therefore require not only deep emission reductions but also large-scale carbon removal solutions. Direct Air Capture (DAC) is one of the few technologies capable of permanently removing CO2 directly from the atmosphere, but significant scientific and engineering challenges remain before DAC can be deployed at gigaton scale. Future DAC systems must be energy-efficient, economically viable, and designed around a fundamental understanding of how materials, processes, and system integration interact.

At Aalborg University, we are seeking ambitious PhD candidates who want to help develop the next generation of DAC technologies through advanced process modelling, experimental studies, and techno-economic evaluations.

The stipend is open for appointment from 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

In the future, removing CO2 from the atmosphere will become an essential part of climate action.
Atmospheric CO2 is already changing the climate. Reducing emissions is essential, but it may not be enough. We must also learn how to remove carbon already present in the atmosphere. Future Direct Air Capture systems will not simply capture CO2:

They will integrate with renewable energy systems. They will operate flexibly and balance the energy systems. They will become scalable climate infrastructure.

What this PhD is really about
The stipends are designed to contribute to two ambitious research initiatives that aim to accelerate the development of Direct Air Capture technologies:

Development of process-aware methodologies for evaluating emerging DAC liquid and solid sorbents and technologies. Development of predictive frameworks linking sorbent properties to process-level DAC performance.

Together, these efforts seek to establish the scientific foundations required to move DAC development from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive, data-driven design and scale-up.

The research environment and culture you will step into
You will join CarbonLab at Aalborg University, a growing research environment dedicated to carbon capture, carbon removal, and climate-positive technologies. We are a group of approximately 20 people currently represented by 7 different nationalities. Our research combines laboratory experiments, process modelling, experimental validation, techno-economic and LCA assessments, and system integration to accelerate the deployment of DAC solutions at scale.

At CarbonLab, we are building more than technologies; we are building a research community. Our researchers share ideas openly, collaborate across disciplines, and celebrate each other's successes. PhD students are treated as colleagues, encouraged to develop their own scientific identity, and supported in taking initiative from the very beginning. Whether presenting at international conferences, contributing to teaching, leading collaborations, or exploring new research directions, you will be part of a culture that combines scientific ambition with mutual trust and genuine support. We believe that excellent research and an excellent research environment go hand in hand.

Your research qualifications
We are looking for highly motivated candidates who are passionate about addressing climate change through scientific research and technological innovation. The ideal candidate has a strong analytical mindset, enjoys solving complex engineering challenges, and is eager to contribute to the development of next-generation carbon removal technologies.

You should hold a master's degree (or be close to completion) in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Energy Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, or a related discipline.

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

Direct Air Capture, carbon capture, or carbon removal technologies Chemical process engineering and process intensification Mass transfer, reaction engineering, and thermodynamics Experimental design and laboratory testing Spectroscopy and related analytical techniques such as Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Measurement and interpretation of gas-liquid and gas-solid equilibrium data and breakthrough experiments. Process modelling and simulation (e.g., Aspen Plus, MATLAB, Python, or similar tools) Data analysis, optimization, and uncertainty assessment Techno-economic analysis and sustainability assessment Energy systems integration and renewable energy technologies

In addition, we value candidates who:

Demonstrate scientific curiosity and creativity Take initiative and ownership of their research Enjoy working both independently and collaboratively Communicate scientific results effectively in written and spoken English Thrive in an interdisciplinary and international research environment Are motivated to contribute to solutions with real-world climate impact

Previous research experience through master's projects, internships, conference contributions, or scientific publications is considered an advantage but is not a formal requirement.

PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

About Valcon

We are a European powerhouse in AI and data-driven business transformation, bringing this to life by integrating management consulting with data and digital technology capabilities.

We ensure companies are in their best possible shape and fit for the future. We spot opportunities and help bring them to life. We are thorough, fast and collaborative in everything we do. From the boardroom to the shop floor. From strategy to operations.

We are a no-nonsense consultancy with curious individuals who are driven by creating value together with clients. We have an informal culture and a flat hierarchy with offices in Denmark, Sweden, the Netherlands, the UK, Germany, Croatia and Serbia.

To thrive in this role, you have demonstrated experience in these three competence areas:

• Commercial growth: Build strong client relationships, identify opportunities and contribute to the growth of existing and new client engagements through trusted advisory and business development activities

• Client engagement: Lead complex supply chain and operational improvement transformations from problem definition and solution design through implementation and value realization.

• Capability development: Help strengthen Supply Chain & Operations offerings, methodologies and market presence while leveraging AI, data and technology as key enablers of transformation

In addition, you should embody these skills:

• Supply Chain & Operations expertise: Deep experience within one or more areas such as Supply Chain Planning, S&OP, Logistics/Distribution, Procurement, Operational Excellence and Supply Chain Transformation

• People leadership: Build strong relationships, inspire teams and create an environment where people feel empowered, supported and motivated to perform

• Commercial and consulting acumen: Combine strategic thinking with a pragmatic delivery mindset and a strong understanding of how to create value for clients and grow trusted partnerships

• Digital mindset: Experience working with data, digital solutions and technology, or a strong curiosity about how these can enable better supply chain performance and business transformation

• Education: Relevant Master’s degree, fluent in English both written and spoken, Danish is a plus

Career opportunities

Valcon is in a significant growth phase supported by acquisitions and capital investment from Rivean Capital and Waterland Private Equity. This supports our ambitious expansion plans – both geographically and in terms of capabilities – with a particular focus on the Nordics and the DACH (German-speaking) region. Therefore, you will have a unique opportunity to help shape the company’s development and gain strategic influence over its future direction.

The role provides internal career development opportunities toward broader leadership roles within the capability or across the broader organisation. With Valcon’s international footprint and focus on complex Supply Chain and Operation projects in the business and technology space, you will gain access to:

• A broad network of colleagues and clients across Europe

• Strategically significant and high-complexity projects

• Opportunities to work with cutting-edge technology, including AI, data and digital technologies

Application

If this role sounds like a good match, we warmly encourage you to apply and share how your experience, strengths and perspective could contribute to the team. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

**Your impact begins here

**As Integration Project Manager, you will coordinate that data from acquisitions reaches the people who need it, when they need it. You will quickly understand the deliverables, form a plan and align stakeholders behind shared priorities and goals. Your work keeps projects moving and builds a stronger approach for future integrations.

**What You’ll Bring

**You combine structured delivery with strong stakeholder management and a practical understanding of data integration. You bring:

• Substantial experience leading complex projects across functions and organisational boundaries.

• A track record of aligning senior stakeholders, clarifying accountability and driving delivery without direct authority.

• Experience translating business needs into coordinated plans and managing dependencies, risks and competing priorities.

• An understanding of data migration or integration, including how business processes, data and IT systems relate to each other.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to make complex topics clear and actionable.

• The ability to take ownership, build trust, create momentum and work through ambiguity, challenging assumptions constructively.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**Experience with M&A integration, pharmaceutical R&D, CMC or Quality.

**What You’ll Do

**

• You will take ownership of the planning, coordination and governance of data integration, and help teams move forward when information is incomplete or circumstances change.

• Establish and drive cross-functional data integration plans with clear scope, milestones, ownership and governance.

• Align business and technical stakeholders on data requirements, priorities and delivery expectations.

• Coordinate dependencies across R&D, CMC, Quality, IT and Business Development.

• Identify and manage risks, issues and resource constraints, and escalate decisions when needed.

• Give senior stakeholders clear updates on progress, risks and decisions.

• Develop and improve ways of working for data integration, applying lessons learned across projects.

**You will join Integration Data Management in Operations and IT Quality, and work closely with colleagues across the business. In Enterprise IT & Quality, colleagues work across the Novo value chain, staying close to stakeholders and helping deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working.

Your closest partners will be colleagues in R&D, CMC, GMS Quality, Enterprise IT and Business Development.. You will manage competing priorities across multiple projects, so success depends on autonomy, sound judgement and the ability to influence without direct authority. Clear priorities, honest conversations and quick decisions will help you move each integration forward.

**What You Can Expect Here

**Our acquisition portfolio creates a varied environment. You will shape how Novo plans and delivers data integration and strengthen our approach for future acquisitions. You will build new skills through collaboration across the value chain, and you will be trusted to take ownership, make your voice heard and perform at your best.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to bring clarity to complex acquisition data integrations, apply for the Integration Project Manager role by 16 November 2026.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. • Complete assigned tasks thoroughly, accurately, and on time
